correctness.rationale: PASS. Normalized coherent-state intensities are probability Gaussians centered at ±a e1. The min of two integrals is bounded by the average, and bathtub rearrangement uniquely maximizes the average; reflection about Re z1=0 equalizes the two integrals. With g_a(x)=log cosh(2ax)−x², g_a′=2a tanh(2ax)−2x has a unique positive critical point only when a>1/sqrt(2); superlevel cross-sections are Euclidean balls. At the midpoint threshold two open components meet in their closures, giving a unique A_c. Integration yields the explicit cross-section formula. Rescaling g_a=μ x²−(1+μ)² x⁴/3+O(x⁶), x∼sqrt(3μ), gives the beta-integral coefficient 3^q Gamma(q)/(sqrt(pi) Gamma(2q+1/2)) and exponent 2q−1/2; scaling by a gives 2/q! at infinity. Recomputed small-μ quadratures in q=1,2,3 with independent code; finite ratios approach the theoretical coefficients; proof covers all q≥1, a≥0, A>0.
